prompt: Write a method that counts the vowels in a string, ignoring case. Complete the countVowels method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Strings are walked one character at a time with charAt(i) inside a loop bounded by length(). Lower-casing the whole string once up front means each character only needs to be compared against the five lowercase vowels, instead of ten cases. A counter variable accumulates the matches, mirroring the standard counting-loop pattern.
hints: Call s.toLowerCase() once so you only have to compare against lowercase vowels.
Loop with for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) and read each character with charAt(i).
Compare the character against 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u' with == and ||, incrementing a counter on a match.
